subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both directions change where sensitive provider OAuth material may be acquired and stored, and automation should not choose that node/gateway credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups through shared loopback semantics.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC or setup flow that moves provider auth material to the gateway store without first consuming tokens into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but keep permissive
options.body: Warn node-host users that auth affects only the local node, accepting the existing wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups through shared loopback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent already authored and verified the maintainer repair direction for this exact remote-node auth guard.
